newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DSM to step up melamine production.
newsitem.headline: DSM to step up melamine production.

text.p: Dutch chemicals group DSM NV said on Tuesday it planned to step up melamine production at its Geleen plant by 10,000 tonnes a year to 185,000 tonnes annually.
"The capacity expansion (via debottlenecking projects), to be completed in 1998, is needed to keep pace with the rapidly expanding market for melamine," DSM said in a statement.
It said the melamine market was currently growing at a rate of some 4-5 percent annually. Melamine is used in manufacturing adhesives, flame retardants and coatings, amongst others.
DSM said its subsidiary DSM Melamine was studying other debottlenecking projects for its plants in Fortier in the United States and Bontang in Indonesia.
DSM melamine was also studying the construction of a new melamine plant with capacity of some 20-30,000 tonnes a year.
"This plant, which will come on stream in the year 2000 and is likely to be built in Geleen (Netherlands), will use new high pressure technology," DSM said.
It said it had recently acquired the global rights to high-pressure technology from Melamine Chemicals of the US, with which it was cooperating in a research and development project.
